newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak 1996 exports to EU grew 17.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak 1996 exports to EU grew 17.1 pct.

text.p: Slovak exports to European Union countries grew 17.1 percent in 1996 and accounted for 41.3 percent of the total, the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Wednesday.
Imports from the EU grew 36.3 percent and made up 36.9 percent of the total.
But the neighbouring Czech Republic remained Slovakia's largest single trade partner, taking 31 percent of exports and 25.4 of imports.
Exports grew most strongly to Germany, by 19.6 percent to 21.2 percent of the total.
The biggest boost in imports was from Russia, supplier of nearly all Slovakia's oil, natural gas and raw materials.
Imports from Russia rose by 36.8 percent to make up 17.7 percent of the total.

The SUSR released details of the 1996 foreign trade balance published last week. The overall deficit widened last year to 64.54 billion crowns, mainly as a result of an increase in imports of cars, fossil fuels and nuclear plant technology from a revised 5.69 billion crowns trade gap for 1995.
Exports in 1996 rose to 270.62 billion crowns compared to 247.54 billion crowns in 1995, a rise of 6.1 percent. Imports rose by 28.5 percent to 335.16 billion crowns.
